statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-123634 is a use after free in the nginx resolver, when nginx proxies to a server name that contains variables and an SSI or mirror subrequest resolves the same name. nginx.org lists 0.6.18 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163925 . The fix, on the stable-1.30 branch and released in 1.30.7, is https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/7426c29f140c330dd6c6cdfeb2943be1978c69e0 , 'Resolver: fix non-current resolve finalization from resolve handler', with https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/338f6231e347c17a07c381802b1bc3c20c55b529 , 'Resolver: report error on CNAME restart failure'. Every nginx-mainline package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI repository (1.28.2-r0 and 1.29.5-r0 to 1.29.8-r9 on x86_64 and aarch64, and 1.29.4-r0 on aarch64) contains no files and only depends on the nginx package of the same version, so it carries no nginx code of its own. Of those nginx packages, 1.29.8-r9 carries the fix and the earlier ones do not. Pending: whether this owner should be recorded as not containing the component, or should follow the nginx package it depends on, which would make it fixed from 1.29.8-r9.

CVE-2026-123634 is a use after free in the nginx resolver, when nginx proxies to a server name that contains variables and an SSI or mirror subrequest resolves the same name. nginx.org lists 0.6.18 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163925 . The fix, on the stable-1.30 branch and released in 1.30.7, is https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/7426c29f140c330dd6c6cdfeb2943be1978c69e0 , 'Resolver: fix non-current resolve finalization from resolve handler', with https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/338f6231e347c17a07c381802b1bc3c20c55b529 , 'Resolver: report error on CNAME restart failure'. For Alpine 3.24, 1.31.9-r5 and 1.31.9-r6 are the nginx-mainline builds of 1.31.9 in the DHI repository, and their nginx binary reports nginx/1.31.9 on x86_64 and aarch64. The builds 1.31.2-r2 to 1.31.8-r5 ship nginx 1.31.2 to 1.31.8, in the vulnerable range with no backport of the fix, and their nginx binary includes the resolver, which is part of the core nginx binary; the earlier 1.29.8-r0, 1.29.8-r1, 1.31.2-r0 and 1.31.2-r1 packages contain no files and depend on the vulnerable nginx package of the same version. We checked these packages against their index checksums. In the nginx binary, ngx_resolve_name_done and ngx_resolve_addr_done change from 383 and 375 bytes in 1.31.8-r5 to 388 and 265 bytes in 1.31.9-r5 and 1.31.9-r6 on x86_64, and from 408 and 396 to 400 and 276 bytes on aarch64. The 1.31.2 to 1.31.8 builds sort above the 1.30.7 stable fix but are still vulnerable, so the range ends at 1.31.9-r5.

CVE-2026-123634 is a use after free in the nginx resolver, when nginx proxies to a server name that contains variables and an SSI or mirror subrequest resolves the same name. nginx.org lists 0.6.18 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163925 . For Alpine 3.23 the DHI repository publishes nginx 1.28.0-r8 to 1.28.3-r11 and 1.29.4-r0 to 1.29.8-r9, with 1.28.1-r0 and 1.29.4-r0 on aarch64 only. All are upstream releases in the vulnerable range, and the nginx binary of each includes the resolver, which is part of the core nginx binary. 1.28.3-r11 and 1.29.8-r9, built on 2026-11-23, are the first builds made from the Alpine 3.23 nginx recipe at its 1.28.3-r9 revision, which carries Alpine's backport of this fix; Alpine lists it under 1.28.3-r8: https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/raw/a14af845e951fd77441e9b05abe617f58088f4f6/main/nginx/APKBUILD . We checked the nginx package of every build on x86_64 and aarch64, each against its index checksum. In the nginx binary, the exported functions ngx_resolve_name_done and ngx_resolve_addr_done change from 383 and 375 bytes to 388 and 265 bytes on x86_64 and from 408 and 396 to 400 and 276 bytes on aarch64 compared with every earlier build, the same sizes as in the upstream 1.31.9 build. The 1.29 builds sort above 1.28.3-r11 and the 1.29 builds before 1.29.8-r9 lack the fix, so the range reopens at 1.29.4-r0, the first 1.29 build, and closes again at 1.29.8-r9.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-123634 is a use after free in the nginx resolver, when nginx proxies to a server name that contains variables and an SSI or mirror subrequest resolves the same name. nginx.org lists 0.6.18 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163925 . The fix, on the stable-1.30 branch and released in 1.30.7, is https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/7426c29f140c330dd6c6cdfeb2943be1978c69e0 , 'Resolver: fix non-current resolve finalization from resolve handler', with https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/338f6231e347c17a07c381802b1bc3c20c55b529 , 'Resolver: report error on CNAME restart failure'. For Alpine 3.24 the DHI repository publishes nginx 1.28.3-r1, 1.29.8-r0, 1.29.8-r1, 1.30.3-r1, 1.30.3-r2, 1.31.2-r0 and 1.31.2-r1 on x86_64 and aarch64, plus 1.28.3-r0 on aarch64, all built on or before 2026-06-23. Each is an upstream release in the vulnerable range with no backport of the fix, and the nginx binary of each includes the resolver, which is part of the core nginx binary. We checked every one on x86_64 and aarch64 against its index checksum: ngx_resolve_name_done and ngx_resolve_addr_done in each nginx binary are 383 and 375 bytes on x86_64 and 408 and 396 bytes on aarch64, unchanged from the older releases. The 1.31.2 builds sort above the 1.30.7 stable fix but are still vulnerable. No fixed build is published under this package name for Alpine 3.24; the fixed upstream releases 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 are published there under the package names nginx-stable and nginx-mainline.

CVE-2026-123634 is a use after free in the nginx resolver, when nginx proxies to a server name that contains variables and an SSI or mirror subrequest resolves the same name. nginx.org lists 0.6.18 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163925 . The fix, on the stable-1.30 branch and released in 1.30.7, is https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/7426c29f140c330dd6c6cdfeb2943be1978c69e0 , 'Resolver: fix non-current resolve finalization from resolve handler', with https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/338f6231e347c17a07c381802b1bc3c20c55b529 , 'Resolver: report error on CNAME restart failure'. Debian fixes it for trixie in 1.26.3-3+deb13u11, DSA-6642-1: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-123634 . The fixed version in this range is the DHI rebuild of 1.26.3-3+deb13u11, the first nginx build in the DHI Debian repository made from that revision; the earlier builds there are rebuilds of 1.26.3-3+deb13u9 and 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 and lack the fix. We checked the nginx and nginx-dbgsym packages of this build and of the 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 rebuild on amd64 and arm64, each against its index checksum. The Debian changelog shipped in the fixed build lists the CVE-2026-123634 backport from 1.30.7, 'defer freeing detached resolver contexts until their callbacks run'. In /usr/sbin/nginx, read through the debug symbols with the matching build ID, ngx_resolve_name_done grows from 853 to 901 bytes on amd64 and from 684 to 732 bytes on arm64, and ngx_resolve_addr_done from 719 to 770 bytes and from 664 to 704 bytes.
